finding.problem: same-side queue ahead mechanically grants target capacity; larger queue can create a larger target even when risk budget and executable unwind depth are unchanged
finding.economic_implication: queue should reduce fill/completion attractiveness rather than increase target capacity; tying target size to queue can increase required clearing flow exactly when completion is less likely
finding.predecessor: closed research PR #417 identified the analogous V6 mechanism but was not merged; the current unified V7 candidate reintroduces the same monotonicity

fresh_public_context.note: This context does not prove queue-coupled sizing caused the current zero completions because the public summary does not expose point-in-time per-leg queue/depth. It makes the V7 source monotonicity an execution blocker that must be tested prospectively on common candidates.

challenger_contract.target_capacity: risk budget plus independently measured cumulative executable unwind depth; never queue ahead
challenger_contract.promotion_rule: no promotion from quoted edge or order count; require positive audited fill-conditioned post-cost PnL under the prospective joint-state contract
